transcript: Tonight I attended a two-hander at Soho Playhouse called It’s Not What It Looks Like. Narrated like a backstory, this play follows two young adults trying to set the record straight. What starts is just a testimonial additionally evolves into a deeper exploration of their lives and their emotional baggage. The way it all unfolds is like a good crime podcast — it's well structured, layered, and the pieces gradually come together as all as revealed in due time. I was very much along for the ride and I really enjoyed the humor in this piece, which I felt largely comes from a self awareness in the writing and the tendencies of the characters. Overall, I found this play simple but effective, and well performed, definitely a worthwhile 90 minutes. It’s running through August 10th at Soho Playhouse. With that, another program for my collection.
